paragraphs.text: What is a headless CMS? It is a content management system that stores and organises content but does not decide how it looks. Instead of building pages with a theme, it delivers content through an API, and separate front ends, such as a website, mobile app or kiosk, display it in their own way.

A traditional CMS joins content and design in one system, which is simple for a single website. A headless CMS separates them, which suits businesses that publish to several channels, need faster websites, or want to change their front end without moving their content.

sections.h2: Strapi vs Sanity vs Contentful and Other Options

paragraphs.text: Which headless CMS should I choose? It depends on budget, hosting preferences, team skills and how editors like to work. Here is how the main options compare.
suits teams that want an open-source CMS they host themselves, with full control over data and no per-user licence fees. It runs on Node.js and is easy to extend with custom fields and plugins.
suits content-heavy brands that want a hosted platform, real-time collaboration and a highly customisable editing studio. Sanity is billed as a service, with a free tier for smaller projects.
suits larger organisations that want an established, fully managed enterprise platform with strong permissions, workflows and support. Licence costs rise with usage and team size.
suits developer-led projects that want an open-source, TypeScript-based CMS that sits closely alongside a Next.js front end.
suits marketing teams that want a visual editor, where they can see and arrange page sections while still using a headless setup.

Strapi vs Sanity vs Contentful is the most common comparison we are asked about. In short: Strapi for control and self-hosting, Sanity for flexible editing and collaboration, Contentful for enterprise governance. Our headless CMS selection consulting turns that general answer into a written recommendation for your business, with costs over three years.

sections.h2: What Headless CMS Services Does Teknoppy Offer?

items.title: Headless CMS Content Modelling
items.text: Headless CMS content modelling is the most important step. We define content types, fields, relationships and rules, such as a "Service" with a title, summary, benefits, FAQs and related case studies. A good model keeps content consistent and reusable across every channel. It also makes future redesigns far cheaper, because content never has to be rebuilt.

items.title: Headless CMS Implementation
items.html: Headless CMS implementation covers setting up the platform, roles and permissions, media handling, preview links, webhooks and integrations with search, analytics and forms. We then build the front end, usually with Next.js or Astro, and connect it to the CMS.

items.title: Headless CMS Preview and Workflows
items.text: Editors need to see drafts before publishing and to know who approves what. We set up live previews, draft and review states, scheduled publishing and role-based approval steps.

items.title: Omnichannel Content Delivery
items.text: Omnichannel content delivery lets one update in the CMS appear on your website, mobile app, in-store screens or partner sites at the same time. Product details, offers and announcements stay consistent everywhere, and nobody has to copy the same update into several systems by hand.

items.title: Headless CMS Localization
items.text: Headless CMS localization manages English, Arabic, Malayalam and other languages in one place, with translation workflows, fallback rules and right-to-left support for Arabic front ends.

paragraphs.html: For WordPress-based projects, see our headless WordPress page. For Shopify stores, see our headless Shopify page.

sections.h2: Is a Headless CMS Good for SEO?

paragraphs.text: Is a headless CMS good for SEO? Yes, when the front end renders complete HTML on the server and SEO fields are built into the content model. We add fields for page titles, descriptions, social images, canonical URLs and structured data to every content type, so editors manage SEO alongside the content itself. Fast front ends also help Core Web Vitals and AI search visibility.

sections.h2: How Much Does a Headless CMS Cost?

paragraphs.text: How much does a headless CMS cost? There are two parts. The CMS itself may be free and self-hosted, such as Strapi or Payload, or billed monthly, such as Sanity, Contentful or Storyblok. Then there is the one-time project cost: modelling, implementation and the front end.
Every project is quoted after discovery, and the quote is fixed for the agreed scope. We also estimate platform and hosting costs for three years, so you can compare options fairly.

items.q: How long does headless CMS development take?
items.a: A company website usually takes 6 to 8 weeks of headless CMS development. Multilingual or multi-channel projects take 10 to 14 weeks. We confirm the timeline in writing after discovery and platform selection.

items.q: Can we move existing content into a headless CMS?
items.a: Yes. We map your current pages and posts to the new content model, import them with scripts rather than by hand, and check every page before launch. Existing URLs are kept or redirected, so search rankings are protected.

items.q: Do we need developers to manage a headless CMS after launch?
items.a: Not for everyday work. Editors create and update content on their own once trained. Developers are only needed for new page types, new integrations or design changes, which is why careful headless CMS development and modelling at the start saves cost later.
